neighbours.label: Mathematical talk about kinds of number: 'negative number', 'imaginary', and most strongly ' i' of 'i.e.' right after 'a real number,'
fire: In school we learn that the square root of a negative number is not real.
Students often ask why you cannot take an even root of a negative number.
Choose a real number, i.e. 4 or -9, and mark it on the line.
Squaring a negative number always gives a positive result.
The solution has a real part and an imaginary part of equal size.
Suppose x is a real number, i.e. it has no imaginary component at all.
The teacher explained that the cube root of a negative number is still negative.
Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.
quiet: In school we learn that the capital of a country is not always its largest city.
Students often ask why the survey drew such a negative response.
Choose a ripe fruit, i.e. a peach or a plum, and slice it thin.
Praising a nervous child always gives a positive result.
The story has a real hero and an imaginary friend of equal charm.
Suppose the tenant is a real person, i.e. not a company or a trust.
The teacher explained that the tone of a negative letter is still polite.
Adding an even integer to an odd integer gives an odd integer.
